newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to lift fishing ban as 1996-97 season opens.
newsitem.headline: Peru to lift fishing ban as 1996-97 season opens.

text.p: The Peruvian government said it would lift from midnight Tuesday a temporary anchovy and sardine fishing ban in line with the beginning of the 1996-1997 season.

A decree in the official daily El Peruano, signed by Fisheries' Minister Carlos Boggiano Sanchez, also specified the fishing quotas for anchovy and sardine in the first quarter of the season between November 1996 and January 1997.

Fishermen can extract up to three million tonnes of anchovy from the north and central waters during this period, and 200,000 tonnes from the southern region. The quota for sardines is 200,000 tonnes throughout all waters.
The decree prohibited the use of sardines in the production of fishmeal.
Peru is the world's second-largest producer of fishmeal, made principally from anchovy.
The government normally imposes two temporary bans on fishing per year, around October and February, to preserve stock.
